*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(-2+3t)\,i+(1-2t)\,j.$*

question.html:
Question 1
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=(x+y)2i+ex−yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(−2,1) to the point B(1,−1)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(−2+3t)i+(1−2t)j.

a
∫01(t−1)2+e5t−3dt
b
∫013t2−2etdt
c
∫013(t−1)2−2e5t−3dt
d
∫012(t−3)2−3e5t−1dt
e
∫01(t−3)2+et−1dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=−2i+j and b=i−j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(−2i+j)+t[(i−j)−(−2i+j)]=(−2i+j)+t(3i−2j)=(−2+3t)i+(1−2t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=−2+3t,y=1−2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=(x+y)2i+ex−yj=(−2+3t+1−2t)2i+e−2+3t−(1−2t)j=(t−1)2i+e5t−3j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(−2+3t)i+ddt(1−2t)j=3i−2j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((t−1)2i+e5t−2j)⋅(3i−2j)=(t−1)2⋅3+e5t−3⋅(−2)=3(t−1)2−2e5t−3.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫013(t−1)2−2e5t−3dt.

feedback.name: Question 1
feedback.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(x+y)^{2}\,i+{e}^{x-y}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(-2,1)$ to the point $B(1,-1)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(-2+3t)\,i+(1-2t)\,j.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=-2\,i+j$ and $b=i-j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(-2\,i+j)+t[(i-j)-(-2\,i+j)] \\  & =(-2\,i+j)+t(3\,i-2\,j) \\  & =(-2+3t)\,i+(1-2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=-2+3t,\,y=1-2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(x+y)^{2}\,i+{e}^{x-y}\,j \\  & =(-2+3t+1-2t)^{2}\,i+{e}^{-2+3t-(1-2t)}\,j \\  & =(t-1)^{2}\,i+{e}^{5t-3}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t)j \\  & =3\,i-2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((t-1)^{2}\,i+{e}^{5t-2}\,j)\cdot (3\,i-2\,j) \\  & =(t-1)^{2}\cdot 3+{e}^{5t-3}\cdot (-2) \\  & =3(t-1)^{2}-2{e}^{5t-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3(t-1)^{2}-2{e}^{5t-3}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=(x+y)2i+ex−yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(−2,1) to the point B(1,−1)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(−2+3t)i+(1−2t)j.

a
∫01(t−1)2+e5t−3dt
b
∫013t2−2etdt
c
∫013(t−1)2−2e5t−3dt
d
∫012(t−3)2−3e5t−1dt
e
∫01(t−3)2+et−1dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=−2i+j and b=i−j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(−2i+j)+t[(i−j)−(−2i+j)]=(−2i+j)+t(3i−2j)=(−2+3t)i+(1−2t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=−2+3t,y=1−2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=(x+y)2i+ex−yj=(−2+3t+1−2t)2i+e−2+3t−(1−2t)j=(t−1)2i+e5t−3j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(−2+3t)i+ddt(1−2t)j=3i−2j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((t−1)2i+e5t−2j)⋅(3i−2j)=(t−1)2⋅3+e5t−3⋅(−2)=3(t−1)2−2e5t−3.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫013(t−1)2−2e5t−3dt.

question.name: Question 2
question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(2,0)$ to the point $B(4,2).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i$ and $b=4\,i+2\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i)+t[(4\,i+2\,j)-(2\,i)] \\  & =(2\,i)+t(2\,i+2\,j) \\  & =(2t+2)\,i+2t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2t+2\,y=2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j \\  & ={e}^{2t}\,i+{e}^{2t+2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+2)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)j \\  & =2\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{2t}\,i+{e}^{2t+2}\,j)\cdot (2\,i+2\,j) \\  & ={e}^{2t}\cdot 2+{e}^{2t+2}\cdot 2 \\  & =2{e}^{2t}(1+{e}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{e}^{2t}(1+{e}^{2})\,dt \\  & =(1+{e}^{2}){e}^{2t}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(1+{e}^{2})({e}^{2}-1) \\  & ={e}^{4}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Evaluate ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=eyi+exj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(2,0) to the point B(4,2).

a
e4−1
b
e4+1
c
e4
d
(e2−1)2
e
(e2+1)2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=2i and b=4i+2j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(2i)+t[(4i+2j)−(2i)]=(2i)+t(2i+2j)=(2t+2)i+2tj,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=2t+2y=2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=eyi+exj=e2ti+e2t+2j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2t+2)i+ddt(2t)j=2i+2j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(e2ti+e2t+2j)⋅(2i+2j)=e2t⋅2+e2t+2⋅2=2e2t(1+e2).

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫012e2t(1+e2)dt=(1+e2)e2t|01=(1+e2)(e2−1)=e4−1

last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i$ and $b=4\,i+2\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i)+t[(4\,i+2\,j)-(2\,i)] \\  & =(2\,i)+t(2\,i+2\,j) \\  & =(2t+2)\,i+2t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2t+2\,y=2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j \\  & ={e}^{2t}\,i+{e}^{2t+2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+2)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)j \\  & =2\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{2t}\,i+{e}^{2t+2}\,j)\cdot (2\,i+2\,j) \\  & ={e}^{2t}\cdot 2+{e}^{2t+2}\cdot 2 \\  & =2{e}^{2t}(1+{e}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{e}^{2t}(1+{e}^{2})\,dt \\  & =(1+{e}^{2}){e}^{2t}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(1+{e}^{2})({e}^{2}-1) \\  & ={e}^{4}-1\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Question 2

Evaluate ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=eyi+exj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(2,0) to the point B(4,2).

a
e4−1
b
e4+1
c

e
(e2+1)2
Submit

EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=2i and b=4i+2j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(2i)+t[(4i+2j)−(2i)]=(2i)+t(2i+2j)=(2t+2)i+2tj,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=2t+2y=2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=eyi+exj=e2ti+e2t+2j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2t+2)i+ddt(2t)j=2i+2j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(e2ti+e2t+2j)⋅(2i+2j)=e2t⋅2+e2t+2⋅2=2e2t(1+e2).

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫012e2t(1+e2)dt=(1+e2)e2t|01=(1+e2)(e2−1)=e4−1

question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2{x}^{7}\,i+{5}^{x+y}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(2,3)$ to the point $B(5,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(2+3t)\,i+(3+t)\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i+3\,j$ and $b=5\,i+4\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t[(5\,i+4\,j)-(2\,i+3\,j)] \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t(3\,i+j) \\  & =(2+3t)\,i+(3+t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2+3t,\,y=3+t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2{x}^{7}\,i+{5}^{x+y}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{2+3t+3+t}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3+t)j \\  & =3\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+j) \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\cdot 3+{5}^{5+4t}\cdot 1 \\  & =6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=2x7i+5x+yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(2,3) to the point B(5,4)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(2+3t)i+(3+t)j.

a
∫01(2+3t)7+55+4tdt
b
∫013(2+3t)7+4⋅55+4tdt
c
∫014(5+4t)7+3⋅52+3tdt
d
∫016(3t)7+54tdt
e
∫016(2+3t)7+55+4tdt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=2i+3j and b=5i+4j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(2i+3j)+t[(5i+4j)−(2i+3j)]=(2i+3j)+t(3i+j)=(2+3t)i+(3+t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=2+3t,y=3+t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=2x7i+5x+yj=2(2+3t)7i+52+3t+3+tj=2(2+3t)7i+55+4tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2+3t)i+ddt(3+t)j=3i+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2(2+3t)7i+55+4tj)⋅(3i+j)=2(2+3t)7⋅3+55+4t⋅1=6(2+3t)7+55+4t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫016(2+3t)7+55+4tdt.

last_observation.name: Question 3
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Line Integrals Over Line Segments
last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i+3\,j$ and $b=5\,i+4\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t[(5\,i+4\,j)-(2\,i+3\,j)] \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t(3\,i+j) \\  & =(2+3t)\,i+(3+t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2+3t,\,y=3+t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2{x}^{7}\,i+{5}^{x+y}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{2+3t+3+t}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3+t)j \\  & =3\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+j) \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\cdot 3+{5}^{5+4t}\cdot 1 \\  & =6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 3
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2{x}^{7}\,i+{5}^{x+y}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(2,3)$ to the point $B(5,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(2+3t)\,i+(3+t)\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i+3\,j$ and $b=5\,i+4\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t[(5\,i+4\,j)-(2\,i+3\,j)] \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t(3\,i+j) \\  & =(2+3t)\,i+(3+t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2+3t,\,y=3+t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2{x}^{7}\,i+{5}^{x+y}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{2+3t+3+t}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3+t)j \\  & =3\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+j) \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\cdot 3+{5}^{5+4t}\cdot 1 \\  & =6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 3
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=2x7i+5x+yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(2,3) to the point B(5,4)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(2+3t)i+(3+t)j.

a
∫01(2+3t)7+55+4tdt
b
∫013(2+3t)7+4⋅55+4tdt
c
∫014(5+4t)7+3⋅52+3tdt
d
∫016(3t)7+54tdt
e
∫016(2+3t)7+55+4tdt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=2i+3j and b=5i+4j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(2i+3j)+t[(5i+4j)−(2i+3j)]=(2i+3j)+t(3i+j)=(2+3t)i+(3+t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=2+3t,y=3+t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=2x7i+5x+yj=2(2+3t)7i+52+3t+3+tj=2(2+3t)7i+55+4tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2+3t)i+ddt(3+t)j=3i+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2(2+3t)7i+55+4tj)⋅(3i+j)=2(2+3t)7⋅3+55+4t⋅1=6(2+3t)7+55+4t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫016(2+3t)7+55+4tdt.

solution.reasoning: With r(t)=(2+3t,3+t), r'(t)=(3,1) and x+y=5+4t. Thus F(r(t))·r'(t)=6(2+3t)^7+5^{5+4t}, integrated from 0 to 1, which is option e. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different problem.

feedback.name: Question 3
feedback.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2{x}^{7}\,i+{5}^{x+y}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(2,3)$ to the point $B(5,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(2+3t)\,i+(3+t)\,j.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i+3\,j$ and $b=5\,i+4\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t[(5\,i+4\,j)-(2\,i+3\,j)] \\  & =(2\,i+3\,j)+t(3\,i+j) \\  & =(2+3t)\,i+(3+t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2+3t,\,y=3+t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2{x}^{7}\,i+{5}^{x+y}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{2+3t+3+t}\,j \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3+t)j \\  & =3\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2(2+3t)^{7}\,i+{5}^{5+4t}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+j) \\  & =2(2+3t)^{7}\cdot 3+{5}^{5+4t}\cdot 1 \\  & =6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6(2+3t)^{7}+{5}^{5+4t}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.html:
Question 3
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=2x7i+5x+yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(2,3) to the point B(5,4)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(2+3t)i+(3+t)j.

a
∫01(2+3t)7+55+4tdt
b
∫013(2+3t)7+4⋅55+4tdt
c
∫014(5+4t)7+3⋅52+3tdt
d
∫016(3t)7+54tdt
e
∫016(2+3t)7+55+4tdt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=2i+3j and b=5i+4j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(2i+3j)+t[(5i+4j)−(2i+3j)]=(2i+3j)+t(3i+j)=(2+3t)i+(3+t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=2+3t,y=3+t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=2x7i+5x+yj=2(2+3t)7i+52+3t+3+tj=2(2+3t)7i+55+4tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2+3t)i+ddt(3+t)j=3i+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2(2+3t)7i+55+4tj)⋅(3i+j)=2(2+3t)7⋅3+55+4t⋅1=6(2+3t)7+55+4t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫016(2+3t)7+55+4tdt.

question.name: Question 4
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+\sqrt{xy}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(1,1)$ to the point $B(4,3)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(1+3t)\,i+(1+2t)\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=i+j$ and $b=4\,i+3\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(i+j)+t[(4\,i+3\,j)-(i+j)] \\  & =(i+j)+t(3i+2\,j) \\  & =(1+3t)\,i+(1+2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=1+3t,\,y=1+2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+\sqrt{xy}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+3t+1+2t)\,i+\sqrt{(1+3t)(1+2t)}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+2t)j \\  & =3\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+2\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\cdot 3+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\cdot 2 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=ln⁡(x+y)i+xyj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(1,1) to the point B(4,3)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(1+3t)i+(1+2t)j.

a
∫015ln⁡(5t)+66tdt
b
∫01ln⁡(2+5t)+1+5t+6t2dt
c
∫015ln⁡(2+5t)+61+5t+6t2dt
d
∫013ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2dt
e
∫012ln⁡(5t)+36tdt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=i+j and b=4i+3j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(i+j)+t[(4i+3j)−(i+j)]=(i+j)+t(3i+2j)=(1+3t)i+(1+2t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=1+3t,y=1+2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=ln⁡(x+y)i+xyj=ln⁡(1+3t+1+2t)i+(1+3t)(1+2t)j=ln⁡(2+5t)i+1+5t+6t2j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(1+3t)i+ddt(1+2t)j=3i+2j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(ln⁡(2+5t)i+1+5t+6t2j)⋅(3i+2j)=ln⁡(2+5t)⋅3+1+5t+6t2⋅2=3ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫013ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2dt.

last_observation.name: Question 4
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Line Integrals Over Line Segments
last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=i+j$ and $b=4\,i+3\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(i+j)+t[(4\,i+3\,j)-(i+j)] \\  & =(i+j)+t(3i+2\,j) \\  & =(1+3t)\,i+(1+2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=1+3t,\,y=1+2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+\sqrt{xy}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+3t+1+2t)\,i+\sqrt{(1+3t)(1+2t)}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+2t)j \\  & =3\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+2\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\cdot 3+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\cdot 2 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 4
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+\sqrt{xy}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(1,1)$ to the point $B(4,3)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(1+3t)\,i+(1+2t)\,j.$*

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=i+j$ and $b=4\,i+3\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(i+j)+t[(4\,i+3\,j)-(i+j)] \\  & =(i+j)+t(3i+2\,j) \\  & =(1+3t)\,i+(1+2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=1+3t,\,y=1+2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+\sqrt{xy}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+3t+1+2t)\,i+\sqrt{(1+3t)(1+2t)}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+2t)j \\  & =3\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+2\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\cdot 3+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\cdot 2 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=ln⁡(x+y)i+xyj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(1,1) to the point B(4,3)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(1+3t)i+(1+2t)j.

a
∫015ln⁡(5t)+66tdt
b
∫01ln⁡(2+5t)+1+5t+6t2dt
c
∫015ln⁡(2+5t)+61+5t+6t2dt
d
∫013ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2dt
e
∫012ln⁡(5t)+36tdt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=i+j and b=4i+3j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(i+j)+t[(4i+3j)−(i+j)]=(i+j)+t(3i+2j)=(1+3t)i+(1+2t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=1+3t,y=1+2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=ln⁡(x+y)i+xyj=ln⁡(1+3t+1+2t)i+(1+3t)(1+2t)j=ln⁡(2+5t)i+1+5t+6t2j.

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(1+3t)i+ddt(1+2t)j=3i+2j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(ln⁡(2+5t)i+1+5t+6t2j)⋅(3i+2j)=ln⁡(2+5t)⋅3+1+5t+6t2⋅2=3ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2.

Finally, we can write the integral as

feedback.name: Question 4
feedback.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+\sqrt{xy}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(1,1)$ to the point $B(4,3)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(1+3t)\,i+(1+2t)\,j.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=i+j$ and $b=4\,i+3\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(i+j)+t[(4\,i+3\,j)-(i+j)] \\  & =(i+j)+t(3i+2\,j) \\  & =(1+3t)\,i+(1+2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=1+3t,\,y=1+2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+\sqrt{xy}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+3t+1+2t)\,i+\sqrt{(1+3t)(1+2t)}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+2t)j \\  & =3\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\,i+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,j)\cdot (3\,i+2\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)\cdot 3+\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\cdot 2 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+5t)+2\sqrt{1+5t+6{t}^{2}}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=ln⁡(x+y)i+xyj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(1,1) to the point B(4,3)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(1+3t)i+(1+2t)j.

a
∫015ln⁡(5t)+66tdt
b
∫01ln⁡(2+5t)+1+5t+6t2dt
c
∫015ln⁡(2+5t)+61+5t+6t2dt
d
∫013ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2dt
e
∫012ln⁡(5t)+36tdt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=i+j and b=4i+3j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(i+j)+t[(4i+3j)−(i+j)]=(i+j)+t(3i+2j)=(1+3t)i+(1+2t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=1+3t,y=1+2t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=ln⁡(x+y)i+xyj=ln⁡(1+3t+1+2t)i+(1+3t)(1+2t)j=ln⁡(2+5t)i+1+5t+6t2j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(1+3t)i+ddt(1+2t)j=3i+2j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(ln⁡(2+5t)i+1+5t+6t2j)⋅(3i+2j)=ln⁡(2+5t)⋅3+1+5t+6t2⋅2=3ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫013ln⁡(2+5t)+21+5t+6t2dt.

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(3,2)$ to the point $B(1,5)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=3\,i+2\,j$ and $b=i+5\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t[(i+5\,j)-(3\,i+2\,j)] \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t(-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & =(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3-2t,\,y=2+3t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-2t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)j \\  & =-2\,i+3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j)\cdot (-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\cdot (-2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\cdot 3 \\  & =-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=exi+ln⁡yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(3,2) to the point B(1,5)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j.

a
∫01e−2t+ln⁡(3t)dt
b
∫01e2+3t+ln⁡(3−2t)dt
c
∫013e2+3t−2ln⁡(3−2t)dt
d
∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt
e
∫01e3−2t+ln⁡(2+3t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=3i+2j and b=i+5j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(3i+2j)+t[(i+5j)−(3i+2j)]=(3i+2j)+t(−2i+3j)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=3−2t,y=2+3t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=exi+ln⁡yj=e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(3−2t)i+ddt(2+3t)j=−2i+3j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j)⋅(−2i+3j)=e3−2t⋅(−2)+ln⁡(2+3t)⋅3=−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t).

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt.

last_observation.name: Question 5
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Line Integrals Over Line Segments
last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=3\,i+2\,j$ and $b=i+5\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t[(i+5\,j)-(3\,i+2\,j)] \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t(-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & =(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3-2t,\,y=2+3t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-2t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)j \\  & =-2\,i+3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j)\cdot (-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\cdot (-2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\cdot 3 \\  & =-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 5
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=exi+ln⁡yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(3,2) to the point B(1,5)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j.

a
∫01e−2t+ln⁡(3t)dt
b
∫01e2+3t+ln⁡(3−2t)dt
c
∫013e2+3t−2ln⁡(3−2t)dt
d
∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt
e
∫01e3−2t+ln⁡(2+3t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=3i+2j and b=i+5j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(3i+2j)+t[(i+5j)−(3i+2j)]=(3i+2j)+t(−2i+3j)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=3−2t,y=2+3t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=exi+ln⁡yj=e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(3−2t)i+ddt(2+3t)j=−2i+3j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j)⋅(−2i+3j)=e3−2t⋅(−2)+ln⁡(2+3t)⋅3=−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t).

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt.

feedback.name: Question 5
feedback.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(3,2)$ to the point $B(1,5)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=3\,i+2\,j$ and $b=i+5\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t[(i+5\,j)-(3\,i+2\,j)] \\  & =(3\,i+2\,j)+t(-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & =(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3-2t,\,y=2+3t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-2t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+3t)j \\  & =-2\,i+3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{3-2t}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,j)\cdot (-2\,i+3\,j) \\  & ={e}^{3-2t}\cdot (-2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\cdot 3 \\  & =-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-2{e}^{3-2t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+3t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.html:
Question 5
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=exi+ln⁡yj and C is the line segment traversed from the point A(3,2) to the point B(1,5)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j.

a
∫01e−2t+ln⁡(3t)dt
b
∫01e2+3t+ln⁡(3−2t)dt
c
∫013e2+3t−2ln⁡(3−2t)dt
d
∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt
e
∫01e3−2t+ln⁡(2+3t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the line segment. The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are a=3i+2j and b=i+5j. So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

r(t)=a+t(b−a)=(3i+2j)+t[(i+5j)−(3i+2j)]=(3i+2j)+t(−2i+3j)=(3−2t)i+(2+3t)j,

where t varies from t=0 (at the point A) to t=1 (at the point B). Thus, along the curve C, we have x=3−2t,y=2+3t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=exi+ln⁡yj=e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(3−2t)i+ddt(2+3t)j=−2i+3j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(e3−2ti+ln⁡(2+3t)j)⋅(−2i+3j)=e3−2t⋅(−2)+ln⁡(2+3t)⋅3=−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t).

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01−2e3−2t+3ln⁡(2+3t)dt.

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-1$ traversed from the point $A(1,1)$ to the point $B(2,7)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=t\,i+(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j,\,1\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=2{t}^{2}-1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-1)j \\  & =i+4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j)\cdot (i+4t\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\cdot 4t \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=cos⁡xi+sin⁡yj and C is the curve y=2x2−1 traversed from the point A(1,1) to the point B(2,7)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=ti+(2t2−1)j.

a
∫12sin⁡t+4tsin⁡(t2−1)dt
b
∫12sin⁡t+4tsin⁡(t2)dt
c
∫01sin⁡t+4tcos⁡(t2)dt
d
∫01cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt
e
∫12cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

r(t)=ti+(2t2−1)j,1≤t≤2.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t,y=2t2−1.

As a result,

F(r(t))=cos⁡xi+sin⁡yj=cos⁡ti+sin⁡(2t2−1)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t)i+ddt(2t2−1)j=i+4tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(cos⁡ti+sin⁡(2t2−1)j)⋅(i+4tj)=cos⁡t⋅1+sin⁡(2t2−1)⋅4t=cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1).

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫12F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫12cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt.

last_observation.name: Question 6
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Line Integrals Over Cartesian Curves
last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j,\,1\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=2{t}^{2}-1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-1)j \\  & =i+4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j)\cdot (i+4t\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\cdot 4t \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-1$ traversed from the point $A(1,1)$ to the point $B(2,7)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=t\,i+(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j.$*

{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j,\,1\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=2{t}^{2}-1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-1)j \\  & =i+4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j)\cdot (i+4t\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\cdot 4t \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=cos⁡xi+sin⁡yj and C is the curve y=2x2−1 traversed from the point A(1,1) to the point B(2,7)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=ti+(2t2−1)j.

a
∫12sin⁡t+4tsin⁡(t2−1)dt
b
∫12sin⁡t+4tsin⁡(t2)dt
c
∫01sin⁡t+4tcos⁡(t2)dt
d
∫01cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt
e
∫12cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

r(t)=ti+(2t2−1)j,1≤t≤2.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t,y=2t2−1.

As a result,

F(r(t))=cos⁡xi+sin⁡yj=cos⁡ti+sin⁡(2t2−1)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t)i+ddt(2t2−1)j=i+4tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(cos⁡ti+sin⁡(2t2−1)j)⋅(i+4tj)=cos⁡t⋅1+sin⁡(2t2−1)⋅4t=cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1).

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫12F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫12cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt.

solution.reasoning: For r(t)=(t,2t^2-1), the endpoints require 1≤t≤2 and r'(t)=(1,4t). Hence F(r(t))·r'(t)=\cos t+4t\sin(2t^2-1), giving option e. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the supplied worked example concerns a different problem.

feedback.name: Question 6
feedback.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-1$ traversed from the point $A(1,1)$ to the point $B(2,7)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=t\,i+(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j,\,1\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=2{t}^{2}-1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-1)j \\  & =i+4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,j)\cdot (i+4t\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\cdot 4t \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2{t}^{2}-1)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=cos⁡xi+sin⁡yj and C is the curve y=2x2−1 traversed from the point A(1,1) to the point B(2,7)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=ti+(2t2−1)j.

a
∫12sin⁡t+4tsin⁡(t2−1)dt
b
∫12sin⁡t+4tsin⁡(t2)dt
c
∫01sin⁡t+4tcos⁡(t2)dt
d
∫01cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt
e
∫12cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

r(t)=ti+(2t2−1)j,1≤t≤2.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t,y=2t2−1.

As a result,

F(r(t))=cos⁡xi+sin⁡yj=cos⁡ti+sin⁡(2t2−1)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t)i+ddt(2t2−1)j=i+4tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(cos⁡ti+sin⁡(2t2−1)j)⋅(i+4tj)=cos⁡t⋅1+sin⁡(2t2−1)⋅4t=cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1).

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫12F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫12cos⁡t+4tsin⁡(2t2−1)dt.

question.name: Question 7
question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+2y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\operatorname{ln}⁡y-x=0$ traversed from the point $A(0,1)$ to the point $B(1,e).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡y-x=0\,⟹\,x=\operatorname{ln}⁡y.
$$

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+t\,j,\,1\le t\le e.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+2y\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+2t\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{t}\,i+j) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot \frac{1}{t}+2t\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t}+2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{e}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t}+2t)\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡t}{2}+{t}^{2}]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =(\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡e}{2}+{e}^{2})-(0+1) \\  & ={e}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

a
e−12
b

c

d
e+12
e

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making x the subject of the equation, we have

ln⁡y−x=0⟹x=ln⁡y.

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

r(t)=ln⁡ti+tj,1≤t≤e.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=ln⁡t,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+2yj=ln⁡ti+2tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(ln⁡t)i+ddt(t)j=1ti+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(ln⁡ti+2tj)⋅(1ti+j)=ln⁡t⋅1t+2t⋅1=ln⁡tt+2t.

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF⋅dr=∫1eF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫1e(ln⁡tt+2t)dt=[ln2⁡t2+t2]1e=(ln2⁡e2+e2)−(0+1)=e2−12

last_observation.name: Question 7
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Line Integrals Over Cartesian Curves
last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡y-x=0\,⟹\,x=\operatorname{ln}⁡y.
$$

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+t\,j,\,1\le t\le e.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+2y\,j \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+2t\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{t}\,i+j) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t\cdot \frac{1}{t}+2t\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t}+2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{e}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t}+2t)\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡t}{2}+{t}^{2}]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =(\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡e}{2}+{e}^{2})-(0+1) \\  & ={e}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making x the subject of the equation, we have

ln⁡y−x=0⟹x=ln⁡y.

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

r(t)=ln⁡ti+tj,1≤t≤e.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=ln⁡t,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+2yj=ln⁡ti+2tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(ln⁡t)i+ddt(t)j=1ti+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(ln⁡ti+2tj)⋅(1ti+j)=ln⁡t⋅1t+2t⋅1=ln⁡tt+2t.

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF⋅dr=∫1eF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫1e(ln⁡tt+2t)dt=[ln2⁡t2+t2]1e=(ln2⁡e2+e2)−(0+1)=e2−12

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making x the subject of the equation, we have

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=ln⁡t,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+2yj=ln⁡ti+2tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(ln⁡t)i+ddt(t)j=1ti+j.

question.name: Question 8
question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y=3{x}^{2}+1$ traversed from the point $A(0,1)$ to the point $B(1,4).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Since $y$ is the subject of the equation, a parametrization is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j,\,0\le t\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=3{t}^{2}+1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =t\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}+1)j \\  & =i+6t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(t\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j)\cdot (i+6t\,j) \\  & =t\cdot 1+(3{t}^{2}+1)\cdot 6t \\  & =t+18{t}^{3}+6t \\  & =7t+18{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(7t+18{t}^{3})\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{7{t}^{2}}{2}+\frac{9{t}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{7(1)^{2}}{2}+\frac{9(1)^{4}}{2})-0 \\  & =\frac{16}{2} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 8
?

Evaluate ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=xi+yj and C is the curve y=3x2+1 traversed from the point A(0,1) to the point B(1,4).

a
10
b
9
c
7
d
8
e
6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Since y is the subject of the equation, a parametrization is given by

r(t)=ti+(3t2+1)j,0≤t≤1.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t,y=3t2+1.

As a result,

F(r(t))=ti+(3t2+1)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t)i+ddt(3t2+1)j=i+6tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(ti+(3t2+1)j)⋅(i+6tj)=t⋅1+(3t2+1)⋅6t=t+18t3+6t=7t+18t3.

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01(7t+18t3)dt=[7t22+9t42]01=(7(1)22+9(1)42)−0=162=8

feedback.name: Question 8
feedback.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y=3{x}^{2}+1$ traversed from the point $A(0,1)$ to the point $B(1,4).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Since $y$ is the subject of the equation, a parametrization is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j,\,0\le t\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=3{t}^{2}+1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =t\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}+1)j \\  & =i+6t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(t\,i+(3{t}^{2}+1)\,j)\cdot (i+6t\,j) \\  & =t\cdot 1+(3{t}^{2}+1)\cdot 6t \\  & =t+18{t}^{3}+6t \\  & =7t+18{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(7t+18{t}^{3})\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{7{t}^{2}}{2}+\frac{9{t}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{7(1)^{2}}{2}+\frac{9(1)^{4}}{2})-0 \\  & =\frac{16}{2} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 9
question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve ${y}^{3}=x+3$ traversed from the point $A(-3,0)$ to the point $B(5,2).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
{y}^{3}=x+3\,⟹\,x={y}^{3}-3.
$$

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =({t}^{3}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{3}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j \\  & =({t}^{3}-3)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{3}-3))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =3{t}^{2}i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(({t}^{3}-3)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =({t}^{3}-3)\cdot 3{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =3{t}^{5}-9{t}^{2}+{t}^{2} \\  & =3{t}^{5}-8{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3{t}^{5}-8{t}^{2})\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{6}}{2}-\frac{8{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{{2}^{6}}{2}-\frac{8(2)^{3}}{3})-0 \\  & =32-\frac{64}{3} \\  & =\frac{32}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making x the subject of the equation, we have

y3=x+3⟹x=y3−3.

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

r(t)=(t3−3)i+tj,0≤t≤2.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t3−3,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+y2j=(t3−3)i+t2j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt((t3−3))i+ddt(t)j=3t2i+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((t3−3)i+t2j)⋅(3t2i+j)=(t3−3)⋅3t2+t2⋅1=3t5−9t2+t2=3t5−8t2

∫CF⋅dr=∫02F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫02(3t5−8t2)dt=[t62−8t33]02=(262−8(2)33)−0=32−643=323

last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
{y}^{3}=x+3\,⟹\,x={y}^{3}-3.
$$

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =({t}^{3}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{3}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j \\  & =({t}^{3}-3)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{3}-3))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =3{t}^{2}i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(({t}^{3}-3)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =({t}^{3}-3)\cdot 3{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =3{t}^{5}-9{t}^{2}+{t}^{2} \\  & =3{t}^{5}-8{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3{t}^{5}-8{t}^{2})\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{6}}{2}-\frac{8{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{{2}^{6}}{2}-\frac{8(2)^{3}}{3})-0 \\  & =32-\frac{64}{3} \\  & =\frac{32}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

Evaluate ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=xi+y2j and C is the curve y3=x+3 traversed from the point A(−3,0) to the point B(5,2).

EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making x the subject of the equation, we have

y3=x+3⟹x=y3−3.

So, the parametrization of the curve is given by

r(t)=(t3−3)i+tj,0≤t≤2.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t3−3,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+y2j=(t3−3)i+t2j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt((t3−3))i+ddt(t)j=3t2i+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((t3−3)i+t2j)⋅(3t2i+j)=(t3−3)⋅3t2+t2⋅1=3t5−9t2+t2=3t5−8t2

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF⋅dr=∫02F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫02(3t5−8t2)dt=[t62−8t33]02=(262−8(2)33)−0=32−643=323

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt((t3−3))i+ddt(t)j=3t2i+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((t3−3)i+t2j)⋅(3t2i+j)=(t3−3)⋅3t2+t2⋅1=3t5−9t2+t2=3t5−8t2

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF⋅dr=∫02F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫02(3t5−8t2)dt=[t62−8t33]02=(262−8(2)33)−0=32−643=323

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2y\,i+{x}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\sqrt{y}=x+3$ traversed from the point $A(-3,0)$ to the point $B(-1,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\sqrt{t}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2t\,i+(\sqrt{t}-3)^{2}\,j \\  & =2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}-3)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j) \\  & =2t\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =\sqrt{t}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =t-5\sqrt{t}+9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{4}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(t-5\sqrt{t}+9)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 10
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=2yi+x2j and C is the curve y=x+3 traversed from the point A(−3,0) to the point B(−1,4)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(t−3)i+tj.

a
 ∫04(t−5t+9)dt
b
 ∫04(t−t+9)dt
c
 ∫04(t+6t+9)dt
d
 ∫04(t−4t+3)dt
e
 ∫04(t+5t+3)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

r(t)=(t−3)i+tj,0≤t≤4.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t−3,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=2ti+(t−3)2j=2ti+(t−6t+9)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t−3)i+ddt(t)j=12ti+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2ti+(t−6t+9)j)⋅(12ti+j)=2t⋅12t+t−6t+9=t+t−6t+9=t−5t+9.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫04F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫04(t−5t+9)dt.

last_observation.name: Question 10
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Line Integrals Over Cartesian Curves
last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\sqrt{t}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2t\,i+(\sqrt{t}-3)^{2}\,j \\  & =2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}-3)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j) \\  & =2t\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =\sqrt{t}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =t-5\sqrt{t}+9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{4}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(t-5\sqrt{t}+9)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2y\,i+{x}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\sqrt{y}=x+3$ traversed from the point $A(-3,0)$ to the point $B(-1,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\sqrt{t}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2t\,i+(\sqrt{t}-3)^{2}\,j \\  & =2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}-3)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j) \\  & =2t\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =\sqrt{t}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =t-5\sqrt{t}+9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{4}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(t-5\sqrt{t}+9)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 10
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=2yi+x2j and C is the curve y=x+3 traversed from the point A(−3,0) to the point B(−1,4)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(t−3)i+tj.

a
 ∫04(t−5t+9)dt
b
 ∫04(t−t+9)dt
c
 ∫04(t+6t+9)dt
d
 ∫04(t−4t+3)dt
e
 ∫04(t+5t+3)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

r(t)=(t−3)i+tj,0≤t≤4.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t−3,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=2ti+(t−3)2j=2ti+(t−6t+9)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t−3)i+ddt(t)j=12ti+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2ti+(t−6t+9)j)⋅(12ti+j)=2t⋅12t+t−6t+9=t+t−6t+9=t−5t+9.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫04F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫04(t−5t+9)dt.
question.knowledge_point: Line Integrals Over Cartesian Curves

solution.reasoning: For 0<t≤4, r'(t)=(1/(2\sqrt{t}),1). Thus F(r(t))·r'(t)=2t/(2\sqrt{t})+(\sqrt{t}-3)^2=t-5\sqrt{t}+9, giving option a. This integrand extends continuously to t=0 despite the parametrization's endpoint derivative singularity. feedback.name: Question 10
feedback.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=2y\,i+{x}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\sqrt{y}=x+3$ traversed from the point $A(-3,0)$ to the point $B(-1,4)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(\sqrt{t}-3)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\sqrt{t}-3,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2t\,i+(\sqrt{t}-3)^{2}\,j \\  & =2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}-3)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2t\,i+(t-6\sqrt{t}+9)\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+j) \\  & =2t\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =\sqrt{t}+t-6\sqrt{t}+9 \\  & =t-5\sqrt{t}+9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{4}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(t-5\sqrt{t}+9)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=2yi+x2j and C is the curve y=x+3 traversed from the point A(−3,0) to the point B(−1,4)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=(t−3)i+tj.

a
 ∫04(t−5t+9)dt
b
 ∫04(t−t+9)dt
c
 ∫04(t+6t+9)dt
d
 ∫04(t−4t+3)dt
e
 ∫04(t+5t+3)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

r(t)=(t−3)i+tj,0≤t≤4.

Thus, along the curve C, we have x=t−3,y=t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=2ti+(t−3)2j=2ti+(t−6t+9)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(t−3)i+ddt(t)j=12ti+j.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2ti+(t−6t+9)j)⋅(12ti+j)=2t⋅12t+t−6t+9=t+t−6t+9=t−5t+9.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫04F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫04(t−5t+9)dt.

question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14222363/assets/00ff3216e6876673a388eb3eaa0e7d02e268f5e679593ebd9fe01e2840099e1b.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+xy\,j$ and $C$ is the arc of a circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin traversed counterclockwise from the point $(2,0)$ to the point $(0,2)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+xy\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=xi+xyj and C is the arc of a circle of radius 2 centered at the origin traversed counterclockwise from the point (2,0) to the point (0,2)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj.

a
∫0π/2(4sin⁡tcos2⁡t−2cos⁡t)dt
b
∫0π/2(4sin⁡tcos2⁡t−2sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt
c
∫0π(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡t)dt
d
∫0π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt
e
∫π3π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t+4sin2⁡tcos⁡t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius 2 centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as

r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj,0≤t≤π2.

So, along the curve C, we have x=2cos⁡t,y=2sin⁡t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+xyj=2cos⁡ti+2cos⁡t⋅2sin⁡tj=2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(2sin⁡t)j=−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj)⋅(−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj)=2cos⁡t⋅(−2sin⁡t)+4cos⁡tsin⁡t⋅2cos⁡t=−4sin⁡tcos⁡t+8sin⁡tcos2⁡t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫0π/2F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫0π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt.

last_observation.name: Question 11
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Line Integrals Over Circles and Ellipses
last_observation.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+xy\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 11
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=xi+xyj and C is the arc of a circle of radius 2 centered at the origin traversed counterclockwise from the point (2,0) to the point (0,2)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj.

a
∫0π/2(4sin⁡tcos2⁡t−2cos⁡t)dt
b
∫0π/2(4sin⁡tcos2⁡t−2sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt
c
∫0π(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡t)dt
d
∫0π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt
e
∫π3π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t+4sin2⁡tcos⁡t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius 2 centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as

r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj,0≤t≤π2.

So, along the curve C, we have x=2cos⁡t,y=2sin⁡t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+xyj=2cos⁡ti+2cos⁡t⋅2sin⁡tj=2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(2sin⁡t)j=−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj)⋅(−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj)=2cos⁡t⋅(−2sin⁡t)+4cos⁡tsin⁡t⋅2cos⁡t=−4sin⁡tcos⁡t+8sin⁡tcos2⁡t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫0π/2F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫0π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt.
question.knowledge_point: Line Integrals Over Circles and Ellipses

solution.reasoning: The counterclockwise arc is parameterized by r(t)=(2\cos t,2\sin t), 0≤t≤\pi/2. Then F(r(t))=(2\cos t,4\cos t\sin t) and r'(t)=(-2\sin t,2\cos t). Their dot product is 8\sin t\cos^2 t-4\sin t\cos t, matching option d. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different problem.

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14222363/assets/00ff3216e6876673a388eb3eaa0e7d02e268f5e679593ebd9fe01e2840099e1b.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+xy\,j$ and $C$ is the arc of a circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin traversed counterclockwise from the point $(2,0)$ to the point $(0,2)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+xy\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr, where F(x,y)=xi+xyj and C is the arc of a circle of radius 2 centered at the origin traversed counterclockwise from the point (2,0) to the point (0,2)?

Hint: Use the parametrization r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj.

a
∫0π/2(4sin⁡tcos2⁡t−2cos⁡t)dt
b
∫0π/2(4sin⁡tcos2⁡t−2sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt
c
∫0π(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡t)dt
d
∫0π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt
e
∫π3π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t+4sin2⁡tcos⁡t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius 2 centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as

r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj,0≤t≤π2.

So, along the curve C, we have x=2cos⁡t,y=2sin⁡t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=xi+xyj=2cos⁡ti+2cos⁡t⋅2sin⁡tj=2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(2sin⁡t)j=−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2cos⁡ti+4cos⁡tsin⁡tj)⋅(−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj)=2cos⁡t⋅(−2sin⁡t)+4cos⁡tsin⁡t⋅2cos⁡t=−4sin⁡tcos⁡t+8sin⁡tcos2⁡t.

Finally, we can write the integral as

∫CF⋅dr=∫0π/2F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫0π/2(8sin⁡tcos2⁡t−4sin⁡tcos⁡t)dt.
